narrativeReportMd:
# ValueSet R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`ValueSet` keeps the same identity and has no local element removals, cardinality reductions, or type removals, but it does have material breaking risk. The highest-impact change is semantic: multiple `compose.include.valueSet` references changed from union semantics in R4 to intersection semantics in R6. There is also a direct validation break for non-BCP-47 designation languages because the local designation `language` binding changed from preferred common languages to required all languages.

## Scope
This analysis is scoped to local `ValueSet` definitions in the supplied R4 and R6 packages. Inherited base-resource and base-element changes are excluded. The R6 StructureDefinition exists at the expected path and remains the same canonical artifact.

## Main migration themes
Migration work is less about removed fields and more about semantics, terminology, and round-tripping. R4 definitions with more than one value in `compose.include.valueSet` need review because preserving R4 union semantics in R6 generally requires splitting the references into separate include blocks. R6 authors can also express metadata, expansion properties, designation additional uses, include-level copyright, and expansion paging/property details that R4 cannot carry natively.

## Highest-impact findings
The union-to-intersection change for `compose.include.valueSet` is the most important runtime risk. R6 expansion property/paging additions and new filter operators are the most important R6-to-R4 representability and codegen risks.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for value-set composition intent and for the changed meaning of `ValueSet.jurisdiction`, because both can remain structurally valid while changing business behavior.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most R6-only fields are optional additions and are understandable evolution, but they are not directly backward-compatible for strict R4 parsers or lossless R6-to-R4 conversion. The union-to-intersection semantic change is the least backward-compatible change because the same wire representation now means something different.

## Follow-up analysis
Base `Resource`/`DomainResource` changes, cross-artifact canonical-resource pattern changes, terminology artifact changes, and operation-specific `$expand` behavior should be reviewed separately.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: The `ValueSet` resource has no local structural removals, but it has one hard validation break in local designation language binding and several high-impact semantic or round-trip risks. The top concerns are `compose.include.valueSet` union-to-intersection semantics, R6-only expansion property/paging structures, and new filter operators that R4 cannot validate. The main uncertainty is operation/narrative behavior not present in the local package.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should focus on preserving expansion semantics and representability rather than filling newly required fields. Review R4 `compose.include.valueSet` arrays with more than one canonical, validate designation language codes against BCP-47/all-languages, decide how to downgrade or extend R6-only metadata and expansion structures for R4, and test strict parser/codegen behavior for new elements and enum codes.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition deltas: both assigned definitions and relevant local terminology artifacts were available. Confidence is medium for narrative-only semantics such as detailed filter value rules and operation behavior because the rendered R6 narrative pages, official diff, Jira/change rationale, and live terminology expansions were not available locally.

findings.title: Multiple compose.include.valueSet references changed from union to intersection semantics

oldState.summary: The element was `0..* canonical`; if multiple value sets were specified, R4 defined the result as the union of all referenced value sets.

semanticText.definition: If multiple value sets are specified this includes the union of the contents of all of the referenced value sets.

oldState.narrativeMd: An R4 include containing `valueSet: [A, B]` selected concepts from A or B.

newState.summary: The element remains `0..* canonical`, but R6 defines multiple referenced value sets in a single include as an intersection.

semanticText.definition: If multiple value sets are specified this includes the intersection of the contents of all of the referenced value sets.

newState.narrativeMd: The same JSON shape in R6 selects concepts common to A and B, not the union.

facts.note: No structural change; the break is semantic.

facts.oldValue: Concepts from any referenced value set
facts.newValue: Only concepts present in all referenced value sets

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 instances remain structurally valid, but expansion behavior can change dramatically without a validation error. A broad union can become a narrow or empty intersection. Conversely, an R6 author can use one include with multiple `valueSet` references to express an intersection that R4 cannot represent with the same element because R4 assigns union semantics to that wire shape.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: ValueSet expansion controls validation and allowed clinical/business codes. A silent change in expansion membership can cause accepted codes to be rejected or unintended codes to be omitted.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow an include to constrain membership to the overlap of referenced value sets.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Preserve R4 union semantics for repeated `valueSet` and add an explicit intersection construct or operator.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of expressing intersections between referenced value sets is reasonable. The breakage level is not: the same unchanged array now means intersection instead of union, so existing R4 definitions can remain structurally valid while producing materially different expansions. A low-to-moderate cost explicit intersection design would have preserved old data and made the new intent visible.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could keep `ValueSet.compose.include.valueSet` as the R4 union operator and add a new field, operator code, or backbone for intersection. That would introduce another set-algebra surface and require terminology servers to implement one more construct, but it would not create duplicate representations for exactly the same fact: union and intersection are distinct operations. The tradeoff is much smaller than silently changing existing value-set meaning.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds model surface and implementation work, but avoids a silent reversal of existing expansion semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 defines multiple referenced value sets as a union.
evidence.quote: If multiple value sets are specified this includes the union of the contents of all of the referenced value sets.

evidence.detail: R6 defines multiple referenced value sets as an intersection.
evidence.quote: If multiple value sets are specified this includes the intersection of the contents of all of the referenced value sets.

evidence.detail: R4 cardinality and type are unchanged at 0..* canonical.
R6 cardinality and type remain 0..* canonical, confirming a semantic rather than structural delta.

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative. If the R4 author intended a union, split the repeated canonical values into separate include entries for R6. If the R4 include also had system/filter/concept criteria, review the intended set algebra before applying a mechanical split.

findings.narrativeMd: `ValueSet.compose.include.valueSet` keeps the same path and cardinality but changes the meaning of multiple values. This is a silent behavioral break for terminology servers, validators, cached expansions, and business rules that rely on expansion membership. The most dangerous cases are definitions that validate successfully in both releases but produce different expansions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an old-valid/new-invalid structural validation break. It is still-valid-but-behaviorally-different for R4-to-R6. For R6-to-R4, an R6 intersection expressed by multiple canonical values in one include is not faithfully representable by the same R4 element because R4 interprets that same array as a union.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory `ValueSet.compose.include` entries with more than one `valueSet`. For each, determine whether the business intent was union or intersection. To preserve R4 union behavior in R6, split values into separate include components where appropriate and regression-test expansion counts and representative validation cases. Do not rely on structural validation alone.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Changing the meaning of an unchanged repeating element is probably avoidable. An explicit intersection construct would have been more backward-compatible, though less compact. Because R6 ballot text chose direct semantic replacement, migrations need human review for intent.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Prioritize real production value-set definitions with `include.valueSet.length > 1`; single-valued uses are unaffected.

findings.title: Designation language binding strengthened from preferred common languages to required all languages

oldState.summary: Optional `code` with preferred binding to common languages; the snapshot also recorded all-languages as a maxValueSet extension.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 common-languages ValueSet enumerates common BCP-47 tags; arbitrary non-common values were not validation errors under a preferred binding.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 validators could warn about non-preferred language codes, but the binding itself did not make them invalid.

newState.summary: Optional `code` with required binding to all-languages version 6.0.0-ballot4 and a starter binding back to common languages.

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R6 all-languages ValueSet includes the BCP-47 system broadly; no live expansion was run.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires designation language codes to be valid members of the all-languages/BCP-47 value set.

facts.newValue: Same content reference remains, so expansion designations inherit the changed language binding

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance that used a custom or malformed designation language code could still be valid because the binding was preferred. In R6, required binding means such a value fails terminology validation unless it is in all-languages. Correct BCP-47 tags should fare better in R6 than under the R4 common-languages starter set.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is primarily validation and localization metadata quality, not direct clinical logic.

justification.inferredGoal: Require language tags to be valid IETF/BCP-47 tags while retaining common languages as a starter set.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the preferred/max binding and add a warning or best-practice invariant for non-BCP-47 language tags.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Requiring interoperable BCP-47 language tags is a reasonable R6 goal, and the affected old-valid cases should mostly be malformed or non-language local codes. A warning-only path would reduce validation churn, but it would not provide the same assurance that designation language values are real language tags.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking alternative would retain the R4 preferred binding, keep all-languages as a maximum or guidance value set, and add a computable warning for invalid language tags. That preserves all R4-valid instances, but leaves a material interoperability tradeoff: systems consuming designations still could not safely assume the element contains a valid BCP-47 tag.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old unusual values, but does not let consumers rely on `language` being a valid language tag.

evidence.detail: R4 binding strength is preferred and valueSet is common languages.
R6 binding strength is required and valueSet is all-languages.
Expansion designations reuse the compose designation structure.
Local terminology artifacts show R4 common languages enumerated selected BCP-47 tags, while all-languages includes the BCP-47 system broadly.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment focuses on the relevant language value. A real instance would also need required ValueSet metadata such as `status`.

findings.narrativeMd: The local designation language binding changed from a preferred common-language list to a required all-language value set. This strengthens validation for both explicitly composed concept designations and expansion designations through the existing content reference.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data with a designation language outside the common list was not invalid solely because of the preferred binding. In R6, a value outside all-languages is invalid. R6-to-R4 representation is mostly safe because R4 can carry the code, though an R4 validator may only treat common-language membership as preferred guidance.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Validate all `designation.language` values against BCP-47/all-languages before R6 migration. Correct malformed local codes or move non-language metadata to an extension. Include expansion fixtures if your system persists `ValueSet.expansion.contains.designation` content.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been less disruptive as a warning, but required BCP-47 language tags improve interoperability. Because the element is optional and invalid custom language codes should be uncommon, the strengthening appears probably justified.

findings.title: Filter operator required value set adds child-of and descendent-leaf

oldState.summary: Required binding to filter-operator 4.0.1; local CodeSystem listed nine operators.

binding.description: The kind of operation to perform as a part of a property based filter.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Compared local CodeSystem concepts, not a live expansion.

newState.summary: Required binding to filter-operator 6.0.0-ballot4; local CodeSystem adds `child-of` and `descendent-leaf`.

binding.description: The kind of operation to perform as a part of a property based filter.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R6 CodeSystem lists both additional codes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 definitions can use two operators that R4 validators and generated enums do not know.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 operator codes are still present, so R4-to-R6 instances are not broken by this binding. The break is in the reverse direction and in codegen: R6-valid instances using the new required-binding codes are invalid in R4 and can fail enum parsing, switch exhaustiveness, SQL mappings, or terminology-server filter dispatch built from R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Unsupported filters can alter expansion membership or make a value set impossible to expand on an R4 terminology service.

justification.inferredGoal: Expose more precise hierarchical filtering operations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; this is a required-binding widening that preserves R4 operator codes and creates only R6-to-R4 downgrade or enum risk.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: All R4 filter-operator codes remain usable in R6, so this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue. The compatibility concern is that R6 instances using `child-of` or `descendent-leaf` cannot be represented or enum-parsed by R4 systems. Adding explicit codes is a proportionate way to add terminology expressiveness.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because R4-valid instances are preserved, backward-compatible alternative availability is not applicable under the calibration rules. Rewriting the new semantics with older operators, extensions, or pre-expanded concepts can be useful downgrade guidance, but those are migration mitigations rather than less-breaking R6 base designs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoiding new codes would reduce R6 expressiveness or overload existing operators; conversion guidance is a mitigation, not a base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 binds to filter-operator version 4.0.1.
R6 binds to filter-operator version 6.0.0-ballot4.
R6 local CodeSystem adds `child-of` and `descendent-leaf`; R4 local CodeSystem does not contain them.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment uses an R6-only operator. An R4 validator with the required R4 filter-operator binding should reject `child-of`.

findings.narrativeMd: The local filter operator binding is still required, but its allowed code set is wider in R6. That is useful for R6 terminology authors but a concrete downgrade and enum compatibility risk for R4 consumers.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is safe for this binding because all observed R4 codes remain present. R6-to-R4 is not safe for instances using `child-of` or `descendent-leaf`; they are invalid against the R4 required binding and likely absent from R4 generated enums.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When downgrading R6 ValueSets, detect the new operators explicitly. If an equivalent R4 expression exists for the target code system, rewrite with documented semantics; otherwise preserve via extension, pre-expanded concepts, or reject with a clear compatibility error. Update enum and switch handling for R6.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding codes is mostly unavoidable when adding terminology expressiveness, but it should be paired with explicit cross-version mapping guidance because required-binding codes are common codegen surfaces.

findings.title: R6 adds many optional canonical-resource metadata and governance elements not present in R4

affectedLocation.newPath: ValueSet.versionAlgorithm[x], ValueSet.copyrightLabel, ValueSet.approvalDate, ValueSet.lastReviewDate, ValueSet.effectivePeriod, ValueSet.topic, ValueSet.author, ValueSet.editor, ValueSet.reviewer, ValueSet.endorser, ValueSet.relatedArtifact

oldState.summary: R4 ValueSet did not define these local metadata/governance elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: Comparable information in R4 had to be represented by existing generic metadata, extensions, Provenance, or external documentation.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional local fields for version comparison, copyright label, lifecycle dates, topics, contributors, endorsers, and related artifacts. `relatedArtifact` has local invariant `vsd-12`.

constraints.human: Related artifact can't be depends-on or composed-of

newState.narrativeMd: All added elements are optional at the top level, but they are first-class R6 data that strict R4 models do not recognize.

facts.newValue: ValueSet.relatedArtifact vsd-12 prohibits type depends-on and composed-of

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not invalidate R4 instances when moving forward. They do, however, break strict R4 parsers when present in R6 JSON and cannot be losslessly represented in native R4 without extensions or external metadata. Generated R4 classes also lack these properties.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Most fields are governance metadata rather than direct clinical code membership, but losing them can affect stewardship, publication workflow, and audit decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Bring ValueSet in line with richer canonical resource governance metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; optional R6 metadata additions preserve R4 instances and mainly affect strict R4 parsers or R6-to-R4 downgrade.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added governance and canonical-resource metadata fields are optional, so they do not make R4 ValueSet instances invalid when moving to R6. First-class R6 elements improve discoverability and consistency for R6 tooling. The cost is real for round-tripping into R4, but that is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using only extensions or external metadata would make downgrade easier for R4 ecosystems, but it would also make the information less visible and less uniform in R6. Since the R6 base additions are optional and preserve R4 instances, the alternative question is not applicable; extension mappings remain appropriate conversion mitigations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions or sidecar metadata can preserve data across versions, but they are migration bridges rather than less-breaking R6 base designs.

evidence.detail: R6 differential includes the listed optional top-level elements; R4 differential does not.
R6 relatedArtifact prohibits `depends-on` and `composed-of` related artifact types.

examples.examplesMd: These R6 properties would need R4 extensions or external metadata when downgrading.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a sizable set of governance fields directly to `ValueSet`. They are not R4-to-R6 breaks because they are optional, but they matter for bidirectional conversion, strict parsers, generated classes, and metadata-preserving migration.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance without these fields remains valid in R6. An R6 instance with these fields is not valid native R4 unless the data is transformed into extensions or omitted. `relatedArtifact` also adds an R6-only invariant for allowed related artifact types.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define an explicit downgrade policy for each added field: preserve with standard/custom extensions, keep in sidecar metadata, or accept data loss. Update serializers, generated model classes, and UI forms to support the new R6 elements.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional element additions are the least disruptive way to evolve the model, but they still need cross-version extension mappings to be lossless for R4 ecosystems.

findings.title: Designation additionalUse added with an accompanying use-required invariant

oldState.summary: R4 designation had `language`, `use`, and `value`; there was no separate `additionalUse` element.
oldState.narrativeMd: A designation could identify at most one coded use in the base R4 structure, aside from extensions.

newState.summary: R6 adds `designation.additionalUse` as `0..* Coding` with extensible designation-use binding and invariant `vsd-11`: additionalUse requires use.

constraints.human: Must have a value for concept.designation.use if concept.designation.additionalUse is present

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can express a primary use plus additional use codes; the primary `use` must be present if any `additionalUse` appears.

facts.newValue: The same content reference means R6 expansion designations also use the enhanced designation shape

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 data is unaffected because the element did not exist and remains optional. R6 data using multiple designation uses cannot be represented directly in R4 without extensions or duplicating designations, and R6 validators will reject `additionalUse` without `use`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Designation use affects display/localization metadata more than core membership, but can matter for user-facing labels.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow one designation to carry multiple use classifications while preserving a primary use.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; `additionalUse` is optional R6 content and its invariant only applies when the new element is used.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of representing multiple designation uses on one designation is reasonable, and the new element does not invalidate R4 designations. The `use`-required invariant constrains only instances that choose the new R6 element. The compatibility issue is reverse conversion and older model support, not a less-breakable R4-to-R6 base design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Repeating designations or using R4 extensions are practical downgrade options, but they are not backward-compatible alternatives to the R6 base design because no R4-valid instance is made invalid by the optional addition. Repetition also risks duplicating text and losing the distinction between a primary and additional use.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions or duplicated designations can help downgrade, but they may lose primary-vs-additional use semantics.

evidence.detail: R6 adds optional repeating `additionalUse` of type Coding.
R6 requires `use` when `additionalUse` is present.

examples.examplesMd: Native R4 has no `additionalUse`; preserving it requires an extension or a carefully documented transformation.

findings.narrativeMd: `additionalUse` is a local R6 content addition under concept designations. It is not a forward structural break, but it changes the designation content model and adds a validation rule coupling it to `use`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid because they cannot contain `additionalUse`. R6 instances with `additionalUse` are invalid if `use` is omitted and are not directly representable in R4. Generated R4 models will not have a field for this data.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When converting R6 to R4, map `additionalUse` to an extension or split into additional designation repetitions only if that preserves semantics for the consuming system. Add tests for `additionalUse` with and without `use`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new element is additive and constrained, which is a reasonable compatibility posture. A pure-extension approach would be more R4-friendly but less discoverable in R6.

findings.title: Composition adds include-level copyright and requested expansion properties

oldState.summary: R4 compose include had no include-specific copyright element and no compose-level property request list.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could express overall `ValueSet.copyright`, but not a per-included-code-system copyright statement or default expansion property list in the base resource.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `ValueSet.compose.include.copyright` (`markdown`) and optional repeating `ValueSet.compose.property` (`string`).
newState.narrativeMd: `compose.property` tells expansion producers which concept properties to return if a client does not override the request; `include.copyright` documents copyright for the included code system/version.

facts.newValue: `compose.property` can request default properties or `*` for all known properties

impact.impactRationaleMd: These optional additions do not invalidate R4 content, but R6 ValueSets can now carry composition metadata and expansion behavior hints that R4 cannot carry natively. Ignoring `compose.property` can change which properties are returned in generated expansions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping copyright can create licensing/compliance risk; dropping property requests can change downstream expansion payloads and decision-support inputs.

justification.inferredGoal: Support per-include copyright and default property inclusion in expansions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; optional `include.copyright` and `compose.property` additions preserve R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Per-include copyright and default expansion property requests are reasonable R6 capabilities. Because both additions are optional, existing R4 ValueSet definitions remain valid in R6. The remaining risk is lossless R6-to-R4 conversion or strict R4 parser behavior.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A pure-extension or operation-parameter approach would be more convenient for R4 downgrade, but it would weaken first-class R6 interoperability for expansion producers and licensing metadata. Under the calibration rules this finding is not an R4-to-R6 breaking base-design issue, so backward-compatible alternative availability is not applicable.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Extensions or operation parameters help R4-era systems, but are less discoverable and are migration mitigations rather than base-design alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 adds include-specific copyright as optional markdown.
R6 adds optional repeating compose property strings.
evidence.quote: A property to return in the expansion, if the client does not ask for any particular properties.

examples.examplesMd: Native R4 has no place for these children. `compose.property` may need to become an `$expand` parameter or extension in R4-era systems.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 composition can now carry information that affects expansion production and licensing notices. That is additive but material for systems that round-trip ValueSets or compare expansion payloads.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is safe because the new children are optional. R6-to-R4 loses data unless transformed. R4 parsers may reject these elements if strict unknown-element rejection is enabled.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve `include.copyright` with an extension or external license registry when downgrading. For `compose.property`, decide whether to translate to expansion operation parameters, persist as an extension, or regenerate expansions using R6-aware tooling.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional additions are relatively safe, but a published cross-version extension would make lossless downgrade much clearer.

findings.title: Expansion adds paging and concept property/subProperty structures

oldState.summary: R4 expansions had identifier, timestamp, total, offset, parameters, contains, and designations but no `next` link and no first-class concept property definitions/values.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 expansion metadata could include parameters, but not a structured property catalog or per-concept property values in the base resource.

newState.summary: R6 adds `expansion.next`, `expansion.property`, `expansion.contains.property`, nested `subProperty`, and required typed `value[x]` children within property/subProperty.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 expansion results can be paged with an opaque next URL and can carry structured per-concept property values including nested subproperties.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Expansion resources are often runtime API outputs. R6 servers can return fields that R4 clients, schemas, and generated classes do not know. If clients reject unknown elements or assume one-page complete expansions, `expansion.next` and property structures can cause runtime failures or incomplete terminology behavior.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropped concept properties can affect display, inactivity, hierarchy, or other metadata used in validation and user interfaces.

justification.inferredGoal: Support richer and paged expansion responses with per-concept property data.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; optional R6 expansion paging and property structures are additive and mainly create R6-to-R4/client compatibility risk.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Paged expansions and typed concept properties address practical terminology-service needs, and the added structures do not invalidate R4 ValueSet instances. R4 clients consuming R6 expansion payloads must update, but that is a cross-version runtime and downgrade concern rather than evidence that the R6 base design could have preserved more R4-valid instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Representing paging and properties only through extensions or side channels could reduce strict R4 parser failures, but those approaches are conversion strategies and would provide weaker uniform support in R6. Since the new content is optional and additive, the backward-compatible base-design alternative question is not applicable.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Extension or out-of-band APIs would ease downgrade but would be less type-safe and less uniform for R6 expansion processing.

evidence.detail: R6 adds optional opaque next URL for expansion paging.
R6 adds expansion property definitions.
R6 adds required typed value[x] for each concept property.
evidence.quote: code, Coding, string, integer, boolean, dateTime, decimal

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates R6 expansion fields with no native R4 equivalents.

findings.narrativeMd: The R6 expansion model is materially richer. This is one of the most likely runtime breakpoints because expansions are serialized across service boundaries and parsed by clients generated from a specific FHIR version.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 ValueSets are not invalidated. R6 expansion instances with the new fields are not native R4 and may fail strict R4 JSON validation. Even permissive clients can behave incorrectly if they ignore `next` and treat a partial expansion as complete, or if they drop concept properties needed downstream.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update expansion clients to recognize `expansion.next` and property structures when consuming R6. For downgrade, either strip with acknowledged data loss, map to extensions, or materialize the needed property information in an R4-compatible side channel. Add tests for paged expansions and property values of every allowed `value[x]` type.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional typed additions are reasonable for R6, but they are not wire-compatible with strict R4 clients. A pure extension design would have been more backward-compatible but less type-safe and less interoperable for property-aware expansion processing.

findings.title: ValueSet.url adds warning constraint against pipe, hash, and space characters

oldState.summary: R4 had no local `cnl-1` warning constraint on `ValueSet.url`.
oldState.narrativeMd: Canonical URL text already discouraged unstable identifiers, but the local constraint was absent.

newState.summary: R6 adds warning constraint `cnl-1`: URL should not contain `|`, `#`, or spaces.

constraints.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

newState.narrativeMd: The constraint is warning severity, not an error, but it formalizes a canonical-reference processing rule.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the new rule is warning severity, it should not make an instance invalid under normal FHIR validation. It can still break pipelines that promote warnings to errors, enforce canonical hygiene during publishing, or rely on URLs with `|`, `#`, or spaces.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Canonical parsing issues can cause broken references, but the rule targets unusual URL forms.

justification.inferredGoal: Prevent canonical URLs from containing characters that conflict with canonical version fragments and reference processing.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking computable base design identified; warning severity already avoids hard invalidation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal is strong: `|`, `#`, and spaces cause real canonical-reference processing hazards. R6 uses warning severity rather than an error, so normal validation preserves R4 instances while surfacing the issue to tooling. Pipelines that promote warnings to errors may need policy changes, but that does not make the base design disproportionate.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The only materially less disruptive base option would be prose-only guidance or no computable rule. That would reduce operational warning churn but would not meet the same tooling goal. A warning constraint is already the compatibility-preserving version of the rule, so no plausible less-breaking base design was identified.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Narrative-only guidance would avoid warning-as-error churn but would be much easier for tooling to miss.

evidence.detail: R6 adds the canonical URL warning.
R4 has no corresponding local warning constraint.

examples.examplesMd: `ValueSet.url` values such as `http://example.org/fhir/ValueSet/foo|bar`, `http://example.org/fhir/ValueSet/foo#bar`, or values containing spaces would trigger the R6 warning.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a computable warning for canonical URL hygiene. This is not a hard breaking change, but it can affect publication gates or validators configured to fail on warnings.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with these characters remain structurally representable in R6. Under standard severity handling they generate a warning rather than an error. Warning-as-error pipelines can experience an operational break.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan canonical URLs and normalize or mint replacement canonicals where possible. Because canonical changes are themselves disruptive, do not rewrite published URLs automatically without governance review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The warning-severity design is an appropriate backward-compatible mechanism for a conformance improvement.

findings.title: ValueSet.jurisdiction semantics shifted from intended use jurisdiction to maintaining authority jurisdiction

oldState.summary: R4 described jurisdiction as a legal/geographic region in which the ValueSet is intended to be used, with extensible binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/jurisdiction`.

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

semanticText.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the value set is intended to be used.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 supported filtering or interpreting a ValueSet by intended jurisdiction of use.

newState.summary: R6 describes jurisdiction as the region in which the maintaining authority operates, with extensible binding to `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/jurisdiction` and a deprecation note encouraging jurisdiction in `useContext`.

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

semanticText.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 shifts primary meaning toward authority/stewardship jurisdiction and points intended-use jurisdictions toward `useContext`.

facts.oldValue: Region in which the value set is intended to be used
facts.newValue: Region in which the maintaining authority operates

impact.impactRationaleMd: The same CodeableConcept values remain structurally valid, but systems that filtered ValueSets by intended jurisdiction of use may misinterpret R6 data if they continue to read `jurisdiction` that way. Conversely, R4 data in this field may need to move to `useContext` to preserve intended-use semantics in R6.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Jurisdiction filters can affect which terminology definitions are selected for regulatory or regional workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify stewardship jurisdiction and encourage intended-use jurisdictions in `useContext`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 intended-use meaning of `jurisdiction` and add a distinct stewardship/authority jurisdiction element or pattern.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying stewardship jurisdiction and promoting `useContext` for intended use are reasonable goals. However, changing the meaning of the existing `jurisdiction` element creates silent semantic migration risk for registries and filters that already use it as intended-use jurisdiction. The supplied evidence does not show why that reinterpretation was necessary instead of adding a distinct stewardship field.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 design could preserve `ValueSet.jurisdiction` as intended-use jurisdiction and introduce an explicit authority/stewardship jurisdiction element, or define a shared canonical-resource pattern for that separate concept. The tradeoff is an extra field and possible long-term duplication of jurisdiction-related metadata, but the two facts are semantically different and the alternative would preserve legacy interpretation much more clearly than redefining the old element.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids silent reinterpretation, but adds another jurisdiction-related metadata surface that could persist and need governance.

evidence.detail: R4 defines jurisdiction as intended use region.
evidence.quote: A legal or geographic region in which the value set is intended to be used.

evidence.detail: R6 defines jurisdiction as maintaining authority region.
evidence.quote: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.

evidence.detail: R6 comment encourages migration to jurisdiction in useContext.
evidence.quote: DEPRECATION NOTE: For consistency, implementations are encouraged to migrate to using the new 'jurisdiction' code in the useContext element.

evidence.detail: R4 binding points to the FHIR jurisdiction ValueSet.
R6 binding points to the terminology.hl7.org jurisdiction ValueSet.

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates the R6 comment guidance; whether to move data depends on whether the R4 value meant intended use or publisher authority.

findings.narrativeMd: `ValueSet.jurisdiction` did not change cardinality or type, but its definition changed materially. This can silently affect registries and governance workflows that use jurisdiction to select applicable ValueSets.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No direct structural validation break is introduced. The compatibility risk is semantic: the same element may be interpreted differently across versions. R6-to-R4 and R4-to-R6 conversions need to decide whether values describe stewardship jurisdiction or intended jurisdiction of use.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit how `jurisdiction` is populated and queried. If R4 values represented intended use, consider moving or duplicating them into R6 `useContext` with usage-context-type `jurisdiction`, while reserving `jurisdiction` for the maintaining authority. Document any profile-specific policy.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Changing the definition of an existing element is less backward-compatible than adding a new stewardship field. The R6 guidance mitigates this by pointing to `useContext`, but migration still requires human interpretation of legacy data intent.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 package did not include a local `ValueSet-jurisdiction.json`; the binding target is external to terminology.hl7.org in the StructureDefinition.

findings.title: Root machine-readable name warning changed to cnl-0 with a stricter pattern

oldState.summary: R4 root warning `vsd-0` checked that `name` matched `[A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){0,254}`.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 warning allowed a one-character name and did not show explicit anchors in the expression.

newState.summary: R6 replaces this with root warning `cnl-0`: if `name` exists, it should match `^[A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){1,254}$`.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 warning is explicitly conditional on name existence, anchored, and requires at least two characters.

facts.oldValue: one initial capital character could satisfy the regex
facts.newValue: initial capital plus at least one additional allowed character

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is warning severity and therefore not a normal hard validation break. The realistic impact is code-generation or publication pipelines that fail on warnings or depend on generated identifiers from `name`.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use the harmonized `cnl-0` warning with the R4-compatible `{0,254}` length rule, and retain or alias `vsd-0` during transition if needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Machine-usable names are a reasonable goal, but the R4 warning already addressed that goal and a single uppercase character can still be a machine-usable identifier. Because the R6 change remains warning-only, impact is low, but the stricter minimum length and abrupt warning-key change are not clearly necessary to meet the goal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could use `name.exists() implies name.matches('^[A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){0,254}$')`, preserving the R4-allowed one-character case while adding anchoring and absent-name handling. If harmonized `cnl-0` naming was the goal, R6 could also retain `vsd-0` as an alias or transitional warning. Duplicate warning keys can clutter suppression lists and may persist, but that is a moderate tradeoff compared with avoidable warning churn.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves one-character names and warning suppressions; tradeoff is slightly weaker harmonization and possible temporary duplicate warning keys.

evidence.detail: R4 root had warning constraint `vsd-0`.
R6 root has warning constraint `cnl-0`.

examples.examplesMd: A single-letter name such as `A` appears to satisfy the R4 pattern but not the R6 pattern. The result is a warning, not an error.

findings.narrativeMd: The machine-readable name constraint was renamed and tightened. It is local to the ValueSet root definition in these StructureDefinitions, but it is low impact because it remains a warning.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Standard R6 validation should warn rather than fail. Toolchains that treat warnings as errors may need to adjust names or severity policy.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Check `ValueSet.name` values used for code generation. Prefer names beginning with an uppercase letter and containing at least two alphanumeric/underscore characters.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A warning constraint is a reasonable backward-compatible way to improve code-generation hygiene.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, baseDefinition, abstract flag, active status, normative status, and FMM level are stable. Publisher/date/package metadata changed as expected for a new ballot package.
No local R4 `ValueSet` elements were removed. R6 adds 33 snapshot element ids, all optional at their parent level except required children inside optional new backbones.

For all 85 common local snapshot element ids, min/max cardinalities were unchanged. New R6 child elements such as expansion property code/value have required cardinalities only when their optional parent backbone is present.
No common local element lost or replaced a type. Existing choice types such as `ValueSet.expansion.parameter.value[x]` retained the same type list.

The local ValueSet differential has no Reference-typed elements with target profiles. Canonical references to ValueSet in `compose.include.valueSet` retained the same structural type while changing semantics.

`ValueSet.status` remains required and local publication-status CodeSystem concepts are unchanged (`draft`, `active`, `retired`, `unknown`). `designation.use` remains extensible to designation-use. Material binding changes are reported separately.

Existing local error constraints `vsd-1`, `vsd-2`, `vsd-3`, `vsd-6`, `vsd-9`, and `vsd-10` retain equivalent FHIRPath expressions. Wording/xpath cleanup and inherited `ele-1`/`ext-1` changes are excluded as base noise. New local constraints are reported separately.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value changes were identified for ValueSet elements.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex value-limit changes were found apart from reported warning constraints on `url` and root `name`.
`ValueSet.status` remains a modifier. No local ValueSet element changed modifier meaning. Apparent snapshot defaulting of `isModifier: false` in R6 is not material.
Local summary flags for existing ValueSet elements are materially stable. The observed R6 summary flag on inherited `modifierExtension` is out of scope.
No local slicing changes were found in the ValueSet differential or relevant snapshot elements.
No representation-format change was found for existing elements. Serialization/codegen risk comes from R6-only elements and enum codes, reported in findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Publication-status binding version changed but local code set is unchanged
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `ValueSet.status` remains `1..1`, modifier, code-typed, and required-bound to publication-status. The local R4 and R6 CodeSystems both contain `draft`, `active`, `retired`, and `unknown`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated enum packages should update the value-set version reference, but no code migration was identified from the supplied local terminology.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Experimental wording now says no version will ever be for genuine usage
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element remains optional boolean with unchanged cardinality and type. The R6 text clarifies a stronger interpretation and says absence is treated as not experimental, but no new constraint was added.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Review governance processes that used `experimental=true` for temporarily pre-production artifacts expected to become genuine later.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Version comment now says business version SHOULD NOT contain #
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is narrative guidance only in the inspected StructureDefinition; cardinality, type, and constraints did not change.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Scan version strings if publication tooling enforces SHOULD-level guidance.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Filter value definition now delegates details to narrative filter-value rules
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: No local cardinality, type, or binding change was found for `filter.value`; it remains required string. The supplied package lacked the referenced narrative page, so no concrete local validation delta was identified.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Consult R6 `valueset.html#filter-values` before finalizing terminology-server filter migration behavior.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: System comment now says contained code systems require the entire canonical URL
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element remains optional `uri` with unchanged constraints. The new text is a conformance clarification rather than a structural change.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Authors of ValueSets that reference contained CodeSystems should verify `include.system` values use the full canonical URL expected by R6.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Several metadata definitions were clarified without structural changes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The inspected elements retain their R4 cardinalities and types. R6 wording clarifies localization guidance, steward/publisher responsibilities, metadata-vs-content date meaning, and copyright as intellectual-property notice.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance and UI labels may need wording updates, but native instance validity is not changed by these text edits.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited base-resource changes, including `Resource.language`, contained resource constraints, narrative recommendations, and extension/base `ele-1`/`ext-1` changes, were explicitly excluded and should be handled by the base artifact reports.
The new R6 filter operator codes are a terminology artifact change with cross-resource impact beyond `ValueSet.compose.include.filter.op`.

Several added governance elements and canonical constraints appear to follow a broader canonical-resource pattern. Cross-artifact reducers should avoid double-counting while still tracking per-resource representability effects.
Expansion paging, returned properties, and `compose.property` are likely coupled to operation-level semantics not assessed in this resource-only report.
